answer: The network builds a reputation reef where each agent must stake a verifiable compute bond before its identity is added to the consensus bridge. Bonds are weighted quadratically, so a single long‑standing node contributes weight 1 while N newly forged identities each add only 1/√N, creating a ripple of diminishing influence. An attacker must therefore allocate proportional resources to match a genuine node’s stake, making a Sybil flood economically prohibitive.
